analyzed_vuln.description: Heap-buffer-overflow in attribute message decoding: H5O_attr_decode computes attr->shared->data_size from decoded datatype and dataspace metadata, allocates that many bytes, then blindly memcpy()s that size from the on-disk object-header message buffer pointer p without verifying that p_size contains enough remaining bytes. With a malformed HDF5 attribute message, this causes an out-of-bounds read from the message chunk during H5Aopen_by_name("MATLAB_class") triggered by matio.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: The PoV is a malformed MAT v7.3 (HDF5) file parsed by matio. Data flow: LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput -> MatioRead -> Mat_VarReadNextInfo73/Iterate -> Mat_H5ReadVarInfo (matio/src/mat73.c) calls H5Aopen_by_name on attribute "MATLAB_class". In HDF5 decoding, attacker-controlled attribute fields (dt_size/ds_size/dataspace extent) make computed data_size exceed remaining bytes in the object header chunk (allocated in H5O__chunk_deserialize). H5O_attr_decode then memcpy()s past the end of that chunk, causing the ASan heap-buffer-overflow read.
